basis: docs/measurement-basis.md#evidence-alignment, published 2026-11-09; definition unchanged for this reading

capture.capture_rule: census of every artifacts/reports/*/experiment.json visible in the local working copy at capture time; sorted by run_id; no random draw and no exclusion by outcome
capture.no_filesystem_probe: The projection never follows a dataset_path to the filesystem. An earlier draft did, which made the frame depend on the capturing machine and produced a path-traversal finding from report content being used as a path. Both the dependency and the finding are gone; every field in the frame is a fact about the report itself.
capture.reproducible_from_checkout: The reading, the frame digest and the four-hop counts are recomputed from the frame alone by scripts/measure_evidence_alignment.py. The fidelity of the projection to the original reports is not independently verifiable from a checkout: those reports are gitignored and only their SHA-256 anchors are shipped.

method: Census of the pinned frame, scored by conclusion. A conclusion is aligned only when every hop resolves in one direction without re-running anything: insight.evidence_ids -> evidence.id, evidence.source_id -> tool_calls.call_id, that call's input is a non-empty object, and the run records both a dataset path and a dataset SHA-256. A broken or empty reference at any hop is unaligned; the gap is recorded with its stage. Runs with no conclusions contribute zero to both numerator and denominator.
denominator_basis: Conclusions, not runs: a run with several conclusions contributes one per conclusion.
diagnostics_scope: Only fields recomputable from the frame belong here. Observations that depended on files present only on the capturing machine were removed rather than reported as if a clean checkout could confirm them; the ledger records them as context. Nothing here enters the numerator or denominator.
scope_note: A full score here is a statement about reference integrity inside the pinned frame, not about the truth of any conclusion, not about content agreement between a tool result and an evidence node, and not about the ability to reproduce a run. It does not change the basis; a new frame or a new hop definition requires a separate reading, with this one left in place and marked superseded.
residual: The frame is a projection. A third party can recompute this reading but cannot verify that the projection faithfully represents the 95 source reports; those reports are gitignored and only their SHA-256 anchors are shipped.

The frame is a convenience census of reports visible in one local working copy, not a random sample of production runs. Many of them are pytest-generated runs and 8 contain no conclusions. The score must not be extrapolated to the deployed system.

Four-hop alignment checks ID references only. It does not compare evidence.result with tool_calls.output, does not check that a cited computation actually produced the claim, and does not assess whether a conclusion is correct.

The fourth hop requires a recorded data hash and path, not a reproducible input. Whether each input still existed was checked once on the capturing machine and is recorded in the ledger as context, not as a field here, because a clean checkout cannot reproduce it. A report that writes a well-formed hash for a lost input still scores aligned.

96 of 96 is a structural property of the report writer, which always emits every field. A report with complete references and wrong content would score identically. This is why the independent-re-run metric exists and remains unmeasured.
series_note: First reading. The two earlier S1 measurements are served-artifact agreement and authorization coverage; this is the third metric, not a repeat of either.
